rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, exceeding one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent paid on or before initial occupancy. This subdivision does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the dwelling of the tenant, except landlords covered by the small-landlord two-month allowance in paragraph (5).

rules.title: Small landlord security deposit cap of two months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and who owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent, may not demand or receive security exceeding two months' rent in addition to the first month's rent. This allowance does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member, and the landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of this.

rules.title: Higher security charged to service members: written statement and return
rules.requirement: On or after April 1, 2025, a landlord charging a service member a higher than standard or advertised security due to credit history, credit score, housing history or other tenant factor must give a written statement of the amount and reason on or before lease signing. The additional amount must be returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears, and the return date must be in the lease.
rules.key_value: return additional security after no more than six (6) months of residency
rules.coverage_text: Service members (as defined in Section 400 of the Military and Veterans Code) renting residential property in which they will reside.
rules.quoted_span: (4) On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged.

rules.title: Limits on deductions from security
rules.requirement: The landlord may claim only amounts reasonably necessary for the defined purposes and may not claim for preexisting damage or conditions or for ordinary wear and tear. Claims must be limited to a reasonable amount to restore the premises to their condition at the inception of the tenancy, and professional cleaning may be charged only if reasonably necessary.
rules.coverage_text: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.quoted_span: (2) (A) The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies.

rules.title: Pre-move-out initial inspection
rules.requirement: The landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the option to request an initial inspection before move-out and, on request, conduct it no earlier than two weeks before termination with at least 48 hours' written notice, then give an itemized statement of proposed deductions. Deductions for repairs or cleanings not identified in the statement are generally barred.
rules.key_value: at least 48 hours' prior written notice; no earlier than two weeks before termination
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies with security for a rental agreement.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply when the tenancy is terminated pursuant to subdivision (2), (3), or (4) of Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
rules.quoted_span: (f) (1) Within a reasonable time after notification of either party’s intention to terminate the tenancy, or before the end of the lease term, the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection.

rules.title: Photograph requirements for security deductions
rules.requirement: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit after possession is returned and before repairs or cleanings to be deducted, and again after they are completed. For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must also photograph the unit immediately before or at the inception of the tenancy.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies with security for a rental agreement.
rules.quoted_span: (2) Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.

rules.title: Return of security and itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of the security and its disposition and return any remaining portion, with copies of documents showing repair or cleaning charges. Documentation is not required if deductions do not exceed $125 or the tenant waived it, unless the tenant requests documentation within 14 calendar days.

rules.exemptions: Documentation need not be provided if deductions for repairs and cleaning together do not exceed $125 or the tenant validly waived the rights, unless the tenant requests documentation within 14 calendar days after receiving the itemized statement.
rules.penalty: The landlord shall not be entitled to claim any amount of the security if the landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply with this subdivision.

rules.title: Security on termination of landlord's interest
rules.requirement: When the landlord's interest in the premises ends, the landlord must within a reasonable time either transfer the remaining security to the successor in interest and notify the tenant, or return the remaining security to the tenant with an accounting.
